title: Tetzaveh: holy on the forehead (Exodus 28:36–38)
hookLine: a gold plate on his forehead reads "HOLY TO THE LORD"

lines: A GOLD PLATE ON THE FOREHEAD.
EVERYONE CAN READ IT BUT HIM.
cards: Where do you put the thing you most need to remember? A sticky note on the bathroom mirror. A word on your phone's lock screen.
People put reminders where their eyes will land. The Torah puts one where the wearer can never see it at all.

In this week's portion, Tetzaveh, the high priest gets a small plate of pure gold, tied across his forehead with a blue cord. Engraved on it, just two Hebrew words. Everyone who looks at him can read it.

teach.h: THE TZITZ: A PLATE OF PURE GOLD.
teach.b: The plate is called the tzitz.
Exodus says to engrave it like a seal, and the words on it, in the old Jewish Publication Society translation, are these: "HOLY TO THE LORD." Then comes a strange line.

The plate shall be on Aaron's forehead, and Aaron shall bear the iniquity of the holy things, the gifts the people bring, so that they may be accepted. It shall be always upon his forehead. So the plate does work.

It carries the mistakes people make even in their offerings, and it has to stay put. Why the forehead? Two days ago we heard the Talmud's list pairing each priestly garment with a wrong it helps atone for.
The forehead plate, it says, is for brazenness, and it ties this to a verse in Jeremiah about a brazen forehead, the way English says someone has a nerve.
The plate sits right where nerve shows, and covers it with holiness. And there's the detail from the hook: the priest can't read his own forehead.
The words face out. Perhaps holiness worn on the face is mostly for the people you meet. They read it in how you look at them, long before you notice it yourself.

how: Tetzaveh is read in synagogue once a year in the cycle of weekly portions, and its description of the high priest's garments, including the gold forehead plate, is studied with it.

o: the gold plate tied across the high priest's forehead
holy to the Lord, the words engraved on the gold
you shall command: the portion of the priest's clothes

games.q: what's inside the plate — tap the pairs.

s: the plate was engraved with Aaron's name
it read holy to the Lord. the tribes' names were on the shoulder stones and the breastplate.
the high priest could not read his own plate while wearing it
it sat on his forehead, facing out, for everyone else to see.
the Talmud links the forehead plate to atoning for brazenness
it ties the plate to Jeremiah's brazen forehead.

games.q: you're designing the last piece of the high priest's clothing. one line of holiness has to go somewhere. where?
o: inside his robe, over his heart.
on a ring on his hand.
games.why: on his forehead, on a gold plate: holy to the Lord. the words face everyone he meets, and never him.

practice: Let a few words come up, gentle, honest, patient, brave, and pick the one you need most. Trace it with a finger on your palm, then touch your forehead lightly, as if placing it there.
You won't see it all day; the people around you might.

wordCard.voice: Tetzaveh. You shall command. The portion that dresses the high priest, ending with a gold plate on his forehead: holy to the Lord.

orig.note: Hebrew: holy to the Lord, the engraving on the gold plate. The divine name is read aloud as Adonai.

carryVoice: Your line: holy on the forehead. The words face out, toward everyone else. See you tomorrow.
